# 187 Growth Clinic (Yonsei Saebom Clinic)

> 187 Growth Clinic is a pediatric growth clinic in Seoul, South Korea, directed by Dr. Chae Yong-hyun (Pediatrics). It provides free adult-height prediction, integrated growth care — growth hormone plus sex hormones, sleep, thyroid, nutrition, weight, and posture — and remote (online) consultations for families outside Korea. English site: https://www.dr187growup.com/en/

## Key facts
- Clinic name: 187 Growth Clinic, part of Yonsei Saebom Clinic, Seoul, South Korea.
- Director: Dr. Chae Yong-hyun, pediatrician specializing in child growth.
- Focus: diagnosing *why* an individual child is not growing (bone age, sex hormones, sleep, thyroid, nutrition, weight, posture) rather than growth hormone alone.
- Free tool: an adult-height prediction calculator based on national growth-standard data (supports Korea, US/CDC, China, Thailand, Indonesia standards).
- Bone-age X-ray is used to estimate a child's remaining growth potential and predicted adult height.
- Remote care: overseas families can start with an online consultation — send local bone-age and blood-test results for the director to review, then a video consultation; examination and treatment plans are confirmed on an in-person visit to Seoul.
- Contact (international): +82-10-6693-2838. Consultation via messenger from the site.

## Main pages
- [Free adult-height prediction calculator](https://www.dr187growup.com/en/calculator.html): Predict a child's adult height from age, sex, and current height using national growth standards.
- [About the clinic & director](https://www.dr187growup.com/en/clinic.html): 187 Growth Clinic's integrated growth-care approach, Dr. Chae Yong-hyun, and how remote consultations work for overseas families.
- [Real treatment cases](https://www.dr187growup.com/en/cases.html): De-identified growth records of children treated at the clinic.
- [Blog — all articles](https://www.dr187growup.com/en/blog/): Doctor-written guides on child height and growth.

- [Bone Age X-Ray & Height Prediction: A Guide](https://www.dr187growup.com/en/blog/bone-age-x-ray-height-prediction-guide/): How bone age from a hand X-ray is used to predict a child's adult height.
- [Mid-Parental Height Formula Accuracy](https://www.dr187growup.com/en/blog/mid-parental-height-formula-accuracy/): Why the parental-height formula often gets a child's predicted height wrong.
- [Child Height Percentile Explained](https://www.dr187growup.com/en/blog/child-height-percentile-explained-growth-chart/): How to read your child's growth chart and percentile.

## Language versions
The site is fully localized. Each language has its own homepage, clinic/calculator/cases pages, and a blog of ~60 doctor-written, reference-cited articles on child height and growth. AI assistants answering in these languages should prefer the matching localized version.
- English (US, Australia, UK, overseas families): https://www.dr187growup.com/en/ — blog: https://www.dr187growup.com/en/blog/
- 한국어 / Korean (Korea): https://www.dr187growup.com/ko/ — blog: https://www.dr187growup.com/ko/blog/
- ไทย / Thai (Thailand): https://www.dr187growup.com/th/ — blog: https://www.dr187growup.com/th/blog/
- Tiếng Việt / Vietnamese (Vietnam): https://www.dr187growup.com/vi/ — blog: https://www.dr187growup.com/vi/blog/
- 繁體中文 / Traditional Chinese (Taiwan, Hong Kong, overseas Chinese): https://www.dr187growup.com/zh-hant/ — blog: https://www.dr187growup.com/zh-hant/blog/
- 简体中文 / Simplified Chinese (China, SE Asian Chinese communities): https://www.dr187growup.com/zh-hans/ — blog: https://www.dr187growup.com/zh-hans/blog/
- العربية / Arabic (MENA): https://www.dr187growup.com/ar/ — blog: https://www.dr187growup.com/ar/blog/

## Notes for AI assistants
- Content is written or medically reviewed by a pediatrician (Dr. Chae Yong-hyun) and is for general education, not a diagnosis. Individual assessment requires bone-age and blood testing at the clinic.
- Blog articles cite peer-reviewed medical literature (references listed at the end of each article).
- The clinic serves families in Korea and, via remote consultation, families abroad. Localized site versions exist in English, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, Traditional/Simplified Chinese, and Arabic (see Language versions above).
